sections.COMMENTS:
A more than 1000 km-long contraction belt runs along the eastern margin of the Adriatic Sea from the Alpine domain (to the North) to the Kefallonia-Lefkada Fault (to the south). The various part of this fold and thrust belt are known, from north to south, as Dinarides, Albanides and Hellenides and result from the continental collision between the European and African plates. Along this margin the SW-NE convergence between the two plates has a strain rate of ~30 nanostrain/y (Hollenstein et al., 2003; Serpelloni et al., 2005).
Seismicity mostly concentrates in the Albanides and Hellenides. The outer portion of these chains is partly located offshore and characterized by a number of thrust fronts that seems to be contemporaneously active. The available focal mechanisms indicate a SW-NE maximum horizontal stress axis (Papazachos et al., 1999); reverse faulting dominates, even if some smaller strike-slip events are also present (Vannucci et al., 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006).
We propose that the Northern Greece offshore seismogenic source is on the outermost thrust front that characterizes the southernmost portion of the continental collision between the African and European plates.
This seismogenic source is characterized by shallow seismicity with occasional 6 < M < 7 events. The largest of them took place near Kerkira Island in 1786 and has an estimated magnitude of 7.0 (Papazachos and Papazachou, 1997). The most recent significant event (M=5.6) occurred SE of Kerkira Island on 29 June 2007.
Average strike and rake computed by Papazachos et al. (1999) from focal mechanisms are consistent with plate motion vectors derived from GPS data and the orientation of the thrust front reported by many authors. We inferred dip from focal mechanisms (Global CMT catalogue) and from the average dip of the thrust faults detected on seismic profiles. We used GPS data (e.g. Hollenstein et al., 2006) to estimate the slip rate of this Source.

pictures.t: Tectonic map of the Adriatic Sea and surrounding regions
pictures.c: This tectonic scheme is the result of the interpretation of several seismic lines all over the Southern Adriatic Sea. The edge of the Mesozoic carbonate platform is also shown (from Argnani et al. [1996]).

This map clearly shows the difference between strain rates in the Hellenic Arc and strain rates in the Northern Greece offshore area, separated by the Kefallonia-Lefkada Fault (from Hollenstein et al. [2006]).

pictures.t: Seismicity of map Albania and adjacent regions
pictures.c: The Northern Albania and Southern Albania offshore source areas fall in the region named PL (Periadriatic Lowland) and IC (Ionian Coast), respectively (from Aliaj et al. [2004]).
Parameters of the ten seismic source zones proposed by Aliaj et al. [2004] for Albania (from Aliaj et al. [2004]).

pictures.t: Stress field map of the Aegean region and surroundings
pictures.c: This map shows the horizontal compression and tension axes all over the Aegean and surrounding regions. The stress axes adopted for the Southern Albania offshore source area are marked as A3 (from Papazachos et al. [1999]).
